# Open Cycling World

**Cross-Platform Indoor Cycling Simulation**

Project Description and Technical Architecture

| 3.74 | **Settings → Trainer → Devices built** (bug report by the user 2026-11-15: "Bluetooth scan for trainer and show is not working. The selection amongst the found devices to select one and then writing it to the default devices.toml is missing."; §3.2.1 *Devices*, §3.4). Cause: the Trainer page's *Scan for devices* and *Show devices* rows ran `devices.scan` / `devices.list`, whose output went only to the closed console; the scan answered only after it ended; nothing let the rider choose a found device; `devices.connect` saved the device before it connected; a connected trainer did not replace the virtual trainer. Now a shared page (`ocw_client::menu::devices`, both apps): *Scan for devices* (10 s, *Stop the scan* while it runs), the devices listed **as they appear** (`ocw_devices::ble::scan_live`) with role (trainer: FTMS or a KICKR by name; power meter; cadence / speed; heart rate), signal and *connected* / *remembered* marks, remembered devices also when not in range; a device's page with kind, state (connecting, connected, failed and why: `DeviceEvent::Failed` with `FailReason` no adapter / not found / connection failed), signal, *Connect* and *Disconnect and forget*. A device is **remembered once it connected** (`devices.toml` in the config dir, or `--devices-file`; a `kind` per device; a file that cannot be written is named in the message), a trainer or power meter replaces the virtual trainer once connected, forgetting the last one brings it back; the HUD marks devices *connecting* / *reconnecting* / *not connected*. The browser's page has *Add a trainer / power meter / heart-rate strap* (its chooser), the same list and device pages, and remembers in `localStorage` once connected. Checked on marge with the Wahoo KICKR |
| 3.73 | **Ride → Join and Ride → Host a ride** (asked by the user 2026-11-15: "in the menu under Ride make an entry **Join** where the user can enter a URL of a server/game/ride he would like to join", and "the menu item Ride → Host a ride where you can select a map and route to host … date/time and weather … start the server on this machine on 0.0.0.0:47800"; §3.2.1 *Shared rides from the menu*, §6.2 *Join links*). **Join links** (`ocw_protocol::join`, pure and wasm-safe): `ocw://HOST[:PORT]?cert=SHA256[&world=ID[@VERSION]][&route=NAME][&name=…]` (port 47800), also `https://HOST:PORT?cert-hash=…` (WebTransport, 47801), a bare `HOST[:PORT]` with the fingerprint entered separately and a pasted `ocw-desktop --server … --server-cert …` line; plain errors ("the certificate fingerprint has 64 hex digits; got 12"); without a fingerprint only `localhost` / 127.x / `::1`. `ocw-server` prints the link(s) (the machine's LAN addresses for an unspecified bind) above "Clients connect with"; `ocw-kiosk.sh` puts them into `server-connect.txt`; `ocw-desktop --join LINK`. **The Ride page** became Events (the four event rows moved to their own page), Workouts, *Join a ride* / *Leave shared ride*, *Host a ride* (or, while hosting, *Hosting – N riders*, *Show join link*, *Stop hosting*), Restart, Back – at most seven items in every mode (`menu::model::RideMode`, items shown by `When`). **Join** (`ocw_client::join::JoinFlow`, `menu::join`, `ocw_ui::join`): a text field row (Enter types, Ctrl+V / ⌘V / the browser's paste event / *Paste link*; a gamepad character wheel), the fingerprint field when needed, Join, the last five servers (`joins.txt` / `localStorage`); the desktop connects in the background with the rider's hello without a world, learns the course from the `Welcome` (10 s timeout), finds the package among the installed worlds (missing: says so, with `--fetch-world URL` for a `world=` manifest URL), asks the trust dialog for an unknown key, loads it through the ride switch, checks the road graph's fingerprint and switches in one frame onto the same connection (the received messages are replayed to the new client); failures keep the ride (timeout, certificate, refusal / sign-in, world missing or another version). *Leave* rides on alone on the same course. The browser joins WebTransport links by starting the page again with `server=` / `cert-hash=` (an `ocw://` link: "no WebTransport … use the desktop app"; `?join=LINK` as a page option). **Host a ride** (`ocw_client::host`: world, route, date and time from the time machine's presets and day steps, weather simulated / real / a preset, bots 0–20 default 5, who changes time and weather, the port; summary, *Start hosting*): the desktop binds `0.0.0.0:PORT` first (a port in use offers to join the server there), keeps the certificate in `<data dir>/ocw/host-tls`, loads the course and runs it **in-process** (`LocalServer::spawn_hosting`: the local server's thread pumps a `NetServer`; no separate binary to package), rides on it as the host and shows the join links with the firewall / port forwarding hint (`host status`, *Copy link* via `arboard`); *Stop hosting* closes it ("server shutting down") and rides on alone with the same time and weather. Console: `join`, `leave`, `ride.join`, `ride.leave`, `join.edit|paste|go|cancel|continue`, `host start|status|stop|copy`, `host.plan`. Open: sign-in required on a hosted server (the row stays hidden until the app has the accounts backend's keys), the browser's join reloads the page (its ride ends then), the in-app world switch while hosting (stop hosting first). |
| 3.72 | The kiosk starts a game server (asked by the user 2026-11-15; §11.2 *Kiosks and deploys*): the deploy installs `ocw-server`, `ocw-kiosk.sh` starts it with the app's world and route, 10 bots, UDP 47800 and a kept certificate, and runs the app as its client, so others can join the kiosk's ride; restarts both on a new build or a crash; `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER=0`, `OCW_KIOSK_LISTEN`, `OCW_KIOSK_BOTS`, `OCW_KIOSK_SERVER_ARGS`; `make test-kiosk` covers it with a fake server |
| 3.71 | **The trust dialog for user keys built** (asked by the user 2026-11-15: "implement showing a dialog that requires trusting the key (show fingerprint)"; §4.7 *User keys*, §12, §14 Phase 16, 16C): a user's own key (`world-builder keys init-user`: a root of their own, its signing key embeds the root's public key in every manifest) is checked with that root, so an intact package by an unknown user key is a new trust failure `UntrustedKey` that **no policy lets through** – the apps ask. The **fingerprint** is the SHA-256 of the raw public key in 16 groups of four hex digits (the key id is its first four); the signer's name is shown as claimed ("signed by 'Ada Rider' (unverified name)"). The **trust dialog** (shared menu model `ConfirmTrust`, both apps, keys / pad / mouse / touch, ten-foot sizes, the fingerprint drawn large): world, id, version, claimed signer, warning, data sources and licences; *Trust this key* (remembered), *Load once* (until the app quits), *Cancel* (focused; Back / Esc / B / closing decline). The **trusted user keys** (`ocw_worldstore::userkeys`: name, key, fingerprint, date, note) in `<data dir>/ocw/trusted-keys.json` (`$OCW_TRUSTED_KEYS`) or the browser's `localStorage`; a corrupt store trusts none and is not overwritten; built-in roots can neither be added nor overridden. *Settings → Account → Trusted world keys* lists and removes them (asks first); `world trust list | add | remove | show | accept | once | decline`. The World menu marks user-signed packages *unofficial, 'name'* or *unknown key, 'name'*. **Shared rides:** the server trusts only what its operator configured (`ocw-server --trust-key`, its account's `trusted-keys.json`; never a client); a client that does not trust the host's new world is asked and leaves the ride when it declines. Bad signatures and files that do not match are refused as before, never asked about. Tests: fingerprint, store, decision, dialog model, the shared-session path, screenshots |
| 3.70 | **T8 memory regression fixed** (§14 Phase 8 T8, *Memory*; Phase 10 B2 / B8a): the vegetation of v3.49 built every chunk's near models (about 100 vertices a tree) for all 25 tiles around the rider – up to 108 MB per Liechtenstein forest tile and 624 MB per Tenerife banana tile – and the tile stream re-queued every tile waiting for its upload in every frame; the browser preview's world rides grew to 2.7 GB of wasm memory (Liechtenstein) or aborted at the 4 GB limit (Tenerife). Now a tile keeps its near plants as recipes and `vegetation::lazy_plants` builds a chunk's near mesh only within 430 m of a camera (detail chunks 250 m) and drops it beyond 530 m (310 m); at most 3 tile builds are pending beyond the urgent ring, none twice. Liechtenstein's ride in Chromium: 3,132 → 432 MB wasm memory; desktop RSS (lavapipe) 4.2 – 4.7 → 2.5 – 3.1 GB, Tenerife 12.0 – 13.8 → 3.8 – 4.1 GB. Budget tests over worst-case tiles; `scripts/test-web.py` fails a world ride above 1,500 MB of wasm memory (`--max-wasm-mb`) |
| 3.69 | Smooth junctions investigated and planned (bug report by the user, 2026-11-15; §4.8.8). Today there is no junction geometry: each road's strip runs flat across to the vertex, ends square there and overlaps the others, so the strips agree only at the vertex point. Measured on Liechtenstein / Black Forest north / Tenerife: visible steps at T junctions with a median of 0.14 / 0.11 / 0.25 m (> 10 cm at 56 / 52 / 85 %, max 1.8–2.3 m, growing with the grade); z-fighting overlaps at about 70 %; verges on the other road at 53–84 %; wedge gaps at 61–77 % of way splits (the roundabout ring in Vaduz: 66 m²). The plan: junction patches built from the road graph (an outline with kerb arcs, a C1 height field, strips trimmed at the mouths, mitred way splits, ridden heights from the same function, the outline dress, markings at the mouths); the renderer first, with no package rebuild (J1a–J1d); profile reconciliation in the builder (J2); roundabouts and complex junctions (J3). Analysis test `junction_seams`, scenes `junction-*`; open questions §4.8.8 Q1–Q5 |
| 3.68 | **The browser app on Safari and iPhones** (§14 Phase 10 B7, B8a; §3.5; the user's report of 2026-11-15: an iPhone 15 on iOS 26 showed the loading screen and played the sound, but drew no image). Safari 26 ships WebGPU on by default, so the page took the WebGPU build. Not reproduced in Safari itself (the Mac build machine has Safari 26.6.2 but no logged-in desktop: neither Safari nor `safaridriver` start from ssh); WebKit's WebGL 2 build rides and draws (Playwright's WebKit, an iPhone 15 emulated). **Fix:** the page's GPU choice moved into `apps/web/web/ocw-gpu.js` – Safari's WebKit (macOS, and every browser on iOS / iPadOS) gets the **WebGL 2 build** (`?gpu=webgpu` still tries WebGPU); a **WebGPU watchdog** (device lost, uncaptured error, `requestDevice` refused, the module not starting, Bevy's renderer error, no frame in 20 s of a visible page, a canvas of one colour once the ride shows) **reloads the ride on WebGL 2** with low graphics and a note, and remembers the failure in this browser (`localStorage`, until the user agent changes); Bevy's renderer errors no longer quit the app but tell the page (`window.ocwRenderFailed`); the start page's *WebGL 2 with low graphics* box is pre-ticked on phones and Safari and finger-sized; `100dvh` for mobile Safari's bars; no pixel-ratio cap in WebKit (it only shrank the HUD there). Tests: `make test-web-gpu` (the rules, three injected WebGPU failures falling back and drawing, the remembered failure, `?gpu=webgpu`, no false alarm, an emulated iPhone), `make test-web-webkit` (`make deps-webkit`), `scripts/test-web-safari.py` for the real Safari once the Mac allows it |

| 3.54 | **The coordinator and the Claude tasks on the build dashboard** (§11.2.1; asked by the user 2026-11-15: "add monitoring of deb to build dashboard", "add info to all running claude tasks to build dashboard"). A **Coordinator (deb)** card at the top of the page (and `coordinator` in `/api/status`, a block in `--once`), read locally from `/proc` and `/sys` without root: memory (total, available, used, swap), the top 5 processes by RSS (name and RSS only, never command lines) and group sums (Claude Code, cargo/rustc, ffmpeg, python, QEMU, browsers), OOM kills (the user journal's unit OOM messages, `/proc/vmstat`'s counter; the kernel log and `dmesg` need root or group `adm` and are marked "not readable"), load against the cores and pressure (PSI), the disks `/`, `/home`, `/home/claude`, `/tmp` when they are their own mounts (deduplicated by device), the sizes of the big directories (du, niced, every 10 min, 60 s limit each), activity (Claude Code sessions, worktrees, ffmpeg, QEMU VMs, the art timer, the dashboard's memory against its `MemoryMax`), and sparklines of the last 6 h (memory available, load, root disk free) from a sample per minute in `test-output/build-log/DAY/deb.jsonl`, read back on start. Alerts with thresholds in one place (`coordinator.THRESHOLDS`): red below 15 % or 2 GiB available, swap above 80 %, a disk above 90 %, an OOM kill in the last 24 h; amber at softer levels. A **Claude tasks** section next to it (`claude_tasks` in the status): the tasks of the coordinator's `agents.jsonl` (running = last event started / resumed; finished ones of the last 24 h behind a toggle), liveness only from the task files' mtime and size (never their content; idle / waiting after 20 min), the worktrees of OCW and OCW-ART with last commit, commits not in `main`, merged and pushed (no fetch), and the **cutover check** ("Cutover OK: no running tasks, no remote runs", or what still runs, with the remote runs from the job queue) for the move of the coordinator to another user |

| 3.43 | **Console Tab completion and the GPS line restored** (§2.9, §3.2). Tab in the console (desktop and browser) completes the word before the cursor: command names, subcommands, long flags and `PossibleValue`s from each command's clap definition, values known only at run time from per-command value providers (`ConsoleAppExt::console_values`: setting keys and values for `set` / `get`, world ids and test routes for `world switch`, the routes and worlds of `ride.switch`, weather presets / subcommands / fields / data sources / days, time presets and speeds, saved `camera.path` files, `help COMMAND`), only commands the session may run (no `dev` commands on a remote server). One rule: one candidate is inserted with a space; several insert their longest common prefix and are listed under the input line, every further Tab inserts the next (Shift+Tab the previous), typing ends the cycle; words with spaces go in quotes. The logic is pure (`ocw_render::completion`, unit tests: prefixes, ambiguity and cycling, subcommands / flags / values, quotes, the permission filter); `console input TEXT` / `console tab` drive it from scripts. **GPS line:** route rides on world packages (desktop `--world PKG --route NAME`, the browser's `?world=…&route=…`) had no GPS line since fae1547 (2026-11-11, route rides on the road graph): `ClientCore::with_route_plan` replaced the route with a placeholder without the package's geographic origin, so the view had no position (free rides and route files kept it; the browser's B6 / B7 shots ride the built-in test route, which has none). The same lost origin hid the latitude / longitude line of the browser's unicorn inspection on a package route (`make test-web-unicorn` checks both now). The placeholder keeps the origin now (regression tests: the view fill sets the position in a route ride, the HUD shows and hides the line). `rider.gps` moved into the shared console (both apps), new `hud.gps on|off` and setting `display.gps` (on); the browser's `?origin=LAT,LON` gives the test route a geographic origin; `make test-web` checks the line and Tab completion (`window.ocw.consoleState()`). |
